titulo: Indirect object pronouns: Me, te and nos: to whom?

aula.objetivo: Say who receives something or who you tell, ask, show or send something to («ele me mandou», «eu te falei», «dei pra ela»), using the spoken forms of Brazil and recognizing the written forms «lhe» and «lhes».

sessao.titulo: Me, te and nos: to whom?

itens.pt: to give (dei = I gave, deu = he/she gave)

blocos.titulo: Who receives? The indirect object: me, te, nos
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the direct object answers «what or whom?» (lesson 23). The indirect object answers «to whom?» or «for whom?»: «Ele me deu um livro» = he gave a book (direct) to me (indirect). English often hides the «to»: «give me a book», but Portuguese keeps the idea. STEP 2: for the first and second person, Portuguese uses the same short pronouns as for the direct object: «me» (to me), «te» (to you) and «nos» (to us). So you only learn one new use for words you already know. STEP 3: in everyday speech in Brazil, «te» is the normal pronoun for «você»: «Eu te mandei uma mensagem.» Many speakers use «você» for the person and still say «te». This is the spoken norm, not a mistake. The written, formal alternative is «lhe» (next session). STEP 4: «nos» is common in writing but speech prefers «pra gente»: «Ele deu um presente pra gente.» STEP 5: for now put the pronoun just before the conjugated verb: «Ela me explicou», «Eu te pergunto», «Ele não me deu». Where else it can go is the topic of the next lesson. STEP 6: when the person is placed after the verb with «pra» or «para», the pronoun is not used: «Ele mandou uma mensagem pra mim» also works, but sounds more emphatic.
blocos.comparacao: In English «She gave me a gift» and «She gave a gift to me» are two patterns. Portuguese has the same two: «Ela me deu um presente» (short pronoun, most common) and «Ela deu um presente pra mim» (with a preposition, for emphasis). Notice that the short pronoun comes before the verb, where English puts «me» after it.

exemplos.ru: Eu te expliquei a regra ontem.
exemplos.pt: I explained the rule to you yesterday.

exemplos.ru: A professora me ensinou muitas coisas.
exemplos.pt: The teacher taught me many things.

tabela.example: Ele nos mostrou a cidade. / Ele mostrou a cidade pra gente.

erros.motivo: In Brazil the short pronoun goes before the verb, not after it with a gap. The next lesson explains the other positions.

erros.errado: Eu mandei a mensagem para te.
erros.certo: Eu te mandei a mensagem. / Eu mandei a mensagem para você.
erros.motivo: «Te» is a short pronoun and does not follow a preposition. After «para» use «você» (or «ti»).
You need a pronoun form (me) to show that «eu» is the person who is asked. Subject forms like «eu» do not work as objects here.

blocos.enunciado: Say five sentences about something someone did for you this week, using «me» and a verb from the list: «Meu amigo me emprestou…», «Minha colega me mandou…», «O professor me explicou…».

Say aloud, using the direct object pronouns from lesson 23: «Eu te vi ontem.» «Ele me conhece.» «Eu vi ela na rua.» Then explain in English the difference between «eu o vi» (written) and «eu vi ele» (spoken).
